$comment: DRAFT ledger for issue #60, one director only (Wong Kar-wai). Same schema as essential10-example.json (schemaVersion 1) with additive fields: format, tmdbYear, sightAndSound2022, rt.reason, rt.alternateCut. Not approved, not for app use until the owner signs off the method and the score-display licensing decision.
methodSummary: Owner decision 2026-11-13: films are ranked by IMDb and Rotten Tomatoes scores. Each film is ranked within this list by IMDb rating and by Tomatometer (ties share the average rank); the two ranks are averaged (ranks, never the raw scores); ties are broken by higher IMDb rating, then more IMDb votes. A Tomatometer with fewer than 10 reviews or no value is ignored and that film is ranked by IMDb alone (flagged rtUsed:false). The film selection is unchanged from the editorial research list; editorialRank keeps the earlier order. Scores are read online and dated, never estimated.

imdb.source: IMDb non-commercial dataset title.ratings.tsv.gz (averageRating, numVotes), matched on IMDb title id; title ids found through title.crew.tsv.gz (director nconst) and cross-checked against TMDB by title, year and runtime
imdb.note: Live IMDb title pages were attempted first and did not return a usable page to an automated request (an empty response, not a human-readable page), so ratings come from the official daily dataset instead; this is the same fallback as the Kurosawa example. The dataset licence is personal / non-commercial use only; see licensing caveats in ESSENTIAL_10_EXAMPLE.md.

rt.source: Rotten Tomatoes film page, critics Tomatometer (scorePercent) and critic review count (reviewCount) read from the page's embedded data
rt.note: Read directly from each film's rottentomatoes.com page with a command-line fetch, one request per page. Percentages and counts are live and change; treat as a dated snapshot. Where a page shows fewer than about 5 reviews no Tomatometer is published and the value is null.

sightAndSound.source: BFI, The Greatest Films of All Time (2022 Sight and Sound poll), positions as listed on the page
sightAndSound.note: The page text was read in two halves; ranks 49-50 and the very bottom of the list were not visible in the extracted text. A film shown without a position was not seen in the portions read; that is not proof it is absent. '=' marks a tie. The page does not state 'critics' poll' in the extracted text, so the figure is labelled 'the 2022 Sight and Sound poll'.

films.title: In the Mood for Love
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).

rt.rtYearNote: RT slug is /m/in_the_mood_for_love_2001; its page lists 2000.

films.rationale: Two neighbours in 1962 Hong Kong, their restraint conveyed through repeated passages, slow motion and a recurring musical theme; fifth in the 2022 Sight and Sound poll and first on both IMDb (8.0 from 192,928 votes) and RT review count (191).

films.title: Fallen Angels
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: Originally conceived as a third story for Chungking Express, then made as a separate film, shot with ultra-wide lenses and neon, at 95% on RT (22 reviews) and 7.5 from 62,011 IMDb votes.

films.title: Chungking Express
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: Two interlocking stories of lovesick Hong Kong policemen shot in handheld bursts and step-printed colour, made quickly between larger projects; second on IMDb (7.9 from 115,106 votes) and the film that made his style widely imitated.

films.title: Days of Being Wild
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Writer).
films.rationale: The first full statement of his themes and visual manner (1960s Hong Kong, missed connections, cinematography by Christopher Doyle) that In the Mood for Love later continues; 91% on RT from 32 reviews.

films.title: Happy Together
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Writer).
films.rationale: A volatile relationship between two Hong Kong men in Buenos Aires, filmed in saturated colour and black and white; Best Director at Cannes 1997.

films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: A sequel in spirit to In the Mood for Love, folding a science-fiction story into the memory of a writer; 7.4 on IMDb from 65,225 votes and 87% from 119 RT reviews.

films.title: Ashes of Time
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay). TMDB 40751 is the 1994 original. The 2008 re-edit 'Ashes of Time Redux' is a separate TMDB film (1610150) and a separate RT page (78% from 78 reviews).

rt.rtYearNote: The 1994 RT page has 3 reviews and no Tomatometer, so the original's RT is null; the Redux figure is given separately and is not the same cut.
rt.reason: RT has not published a Tomatometer for this page (only 3 reviews read).

alternateCut.title: Ashes of Time Redux (2008 re-edit, TMDB 1610150)
alternateCut.note: Different cut from the ranked 1994 film; shown for context only, never to replace the original's null.

films.rationale: His wuxia anti-epic, a swordsman's tale of memory and regret that reinvented the genre's look; evidence for the original is thin on RT, so the 2008 Redux figure (78% from 78 reviews) is shown separately.

films.title: The Grandmaster
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director per TMDB crew (Director, Screenplay).
films.rationale: A kung fu film about Ip Man and the end of an era, with fight choreography treated as portraiture; Oscar-nominated for cinematography and 78% from 139 reviews. The weakest IMDb score in the list (6.6), kept as his one large-scale later film.

nearMisses.title: As Tears Go By
nearMisses.reason: His debut; IMDb 7.0 from 14,560 votes and RT 83% from 12 reviews; not stronger than Ashes of Time or The Grandmaster.

nearMisses.title: Ashes of Time Redux
nearMisses.reason: The 2008 re-edit; a different cut of Ashes of Time (#7), not ranked separately. The IMDb dataset has no separate title for the re-edit, so IMDb's single Ashes of Time entry (tt0109688) may blend votes for both cuts.

nearMisses.title: My Blueberry Nights
nearMisses.reason: His English-language film; RT 47% from 122 reviews, IMDb 6.6 from 59,217 votes.

nearMisses.title: Eros (segment 'The Hand')
nearMisses.reason: Anthology segment, co-credited with Steven Soderbergh and Michelangelo Antonioni; not a feature in its own right.

nearMisses.title: Other 2021-2025 TMDB entries (for example 'Hao Jiu Bu Jian' 1759201 and 'The Hand' 846716)
nearMisses.reason: Not examined individually; they were not treated as eligible standard features.

unverified: RT pages are found under /m/in_the_mood_for_love_2001, /m/fallen_angels_hong_kong and /m/1083093-happy_together; the IMDb director name appears as 'Wong Kar-Wai' (nm0939182) and RT shows 'Kar-Wai Wong'.

Ashes of Time: 1994 original (TMDB 40751) is ranked with IMDb 7.0; its RT page has only 3 reviews so RT is null for the original and the 2008 Redux page (78% from 78) is recorded separately. They are different cuts.
IMDb has one Ashes of Time entry (tt0109688) with no separate Redux title, so its 7.0 / 18,532 votes may blend both cuts.

TMDB credits for Wong include shorts, commercials, an anthology segment and several 2021-2025 entries (for example 'In the Mood for Love 2001', TMDB 1430370, which looks like a re-release listing) that were not examined individually; none was treated as a separate feature.
